Holly lookahead · user experience

The Object Lens: Holly follows the object, wherever you are

Analysts think in objects and events. Holly is organised by data source. This proposal makes every catalogue number and NOTSO number in Holly a doorway to that object's whole story, opened in place, in one click or 4 keystrokes.

17 November 2026Status: approved, both phases, 18 November 2026Prototype: built 17 November 2026Baseline: V0.19All images: synthetic data
Contents Decision neededThe problemOne question, two journeysThe proposalHow it worksOptions and scoringRisksPlan and costHow we will knowPrototype and testOut of scopeOpen questions

Bottom lineRecommendation: build Phase 1 of the Object Lens as V0.20

Phase 1 turns object numbers into links, adds a lens drawer that opens an object's story over any page, and a find-anything palette on Ctrl K (⌘K on a Mac). It reuses the story V0.19 already builds, adds no data, no model and no new permissions, and can be removed without trace. Phase 2, a personal watch list with "since you last looked", follows only if a short hallway test of Phase 1 shows the gain.

InferenceThe roadmap's V0.20 (guided flows and the template synopsis) waits on the local-model decision that is still open. The lens does not, so it can ship while that question is settled.

Owner decision, 18 November 2026: implement both phases now. The hallway test is no longer a gate on Phase 2; the prototype stays available to run it.

Decisions for you

  1. Approve Phase 1 as V0.20, moving the roadmap's V0.20 to V0.21.Alternative: build it after the synopsis work, accepting the delay.
  2. Run the hallway test first? 3 analysts, 5 timed questions, with synthetic data, on the working prototype in section 09, before any production code.Recommended. It costs an hour of analyst time and tests the core assumption.
  3. Links on by default? Numbers become links everywhere, with a switch beside Scanlines to turn them off.Recommended: on, with the switch.

01 · The problemThe same object lives in 6 places, and none of them link to each other

A watch analyst's question is almost always about one object: is it manoeuvring, what did the provider see, what did the floor say, what is due next. Holly holds all of that. It is spread across tabs that each show one source.

4separate search boxes (Notifications, Maneuvers, Comms, Handover), none sharedFactNotificationsLive.tsx:184, ManeuversLive.tsx:282, CommsFeed.tsx, ObjectRail.tsx
0links from chat, the Handover story, timers or the shift log to the object they nameFactthe only cross-page links open a notice (NoticeRow, FeedItem, ManeuverDrawer)
0keyboard shortcuts or global searchFactno key handler in the interface beyond enabling alerts

V0.19's Handover tab already assembles an object's story from every source. InferenceIt is a destination: you must leave what you are reading, open the tab and find the object again. The lens brings that same story to wherever the number appears.

02 · One question, two journeys"What is going on with 90762 right now?"

Today

5 pages

Factwalked in the current interface with synthetic data

  1. Dashboard: find the notice, open it.
  2. Maneuvers: type 90762, scan the records.
  3. Comms: type 90762, read the hits, guess which thread matters.
  4. Handover: find the object in the rail, open its story.
  5. Shift log: scroll to the timers to see what is due.

About 10 to 12 actions and 4 typed searches, and the analyst holds the picture in their head.

With the lens

1 click

Inferencefrom the prototype

  1. Click 90762 wherever it appears (a chat line, a notice, a timer), or press Ctrl K and type 9076, then Enter.
  2. Read: the next timer, every source on one 5-day strip, and what is new since you last looked.

The page underneath stays where it was. Esc returns to it.

SpeculationThe time saved per question is not measured. The hallway test in section 09 measures it before any build.

03 · The proposalThree parts that work as one

The bold move is a change of model, not of screen: Holly treats the object as the thing you navigate by, and every page becomes a way in.

1 · The lens, opened in place

  • A drawer slides over the page you are on. Nothing navigates away.
  • Next due first: the soonest timer for the object, with a countdown.
  • Every source on one strip: notices, provider records, chat, notes and timers as 5 lanes over the window, with a now line.
  • Since you last looked (Phase 2): new items above a marker, older items below.
  • Every item keeps its source label, as the Handover story does today.
  • Actions: open the full story, add a note, set a timer, pin to watch.

2 · Find anything: Ctrl K

  • One box replaces 4 searches for the common case. Type a catalogue number, a name, a NOTSO number or a word.
  • Results grouped: objects first, then notices, then chat, then actions.
  • Each object result says why it matters: open notices, urgency, the next timer.
  • Keyboard first: arrows, Enter opens the lens, Shift Enter pins to watch.
  • The page search boxes stay for filtering within a page.

3 · Numbers become links

  • Every catalogue number and NOTSO number Holly recognises becomes a link chip: in chat, notices, maneuvers, the Handover story, timers and the shift log.
  • Recognised means a whole number that matches an object in the window, the same rule V0.19's server uses for chat, so a clock time or a distance is never linked.
  • On watch (Phase 2): pin the objects you are tracking; each pin shows new items and its next timer.

On a phone

The lens becomes a bottom sheet; the palette fills the width.

04 · How it worksPhase 1 reads only what Holly already serves

RecogniseA number on any page is matched against the window's objects from /handover/objects.
OpenThe lens calls /handover/objects/{sat_no}, the V0.19 story, with its caps, its switched-off channel rule and its sources.
FindThe palette filters objects and notices the page already holds, and asks /mattermost/messages?q= for chat.
Phase 2 onlyA per-user watch list and a last-seen time per object: one table, migration 0021, 3 routes.
  • FactThe story endpoint already applies the rules the lens needs: chat only from channels not switched off, every item with its source, caps that say when part is shown.
  • FactEvery signed-in user can already see everything the lens shows. Phase 1 changes no permission and stores nothing.
  • FactNo language model and nothing outside Holly. The owner's decision of 6 November 2026 is untouched, and the existing no-outside-AI guard keeps covering the server.
  • InferencePhase 2's watch list could live in the browser instead of the server. That would be cheaper, but a pin would not follow an analyst between machines or shifts, which is the point of a watch list.

05 · Options and scoring4 options, weighted; move the weights and see if the answer holds

Scores run from 1 (poor) to 5 (best); for cost and risk, 5 means cheapest or safest. InferenceThe scores are judgement, set out so you can challenge them.

OptionTime to answerBuild costDelivery riskReversibleSecurity and dataTraining loadWeighted

Why not a global search only (B)?

It fixes finding but not reading: you still land on 4 pages to assemble the picture. It is a subset of the lens, so it is included as part 2.

Why not redesign around objects (D)?

Replacing the source tabs with one object board is the bolder idea, but it throws away pages analysts know and the gates have hardened, and needs retraining. The lens gets most of the gain while keeping every page. D stays open if the lens proves the model.

InferenceThe lens leads whenever "time to answer" carries more than about 16 of 100 points against doing nothing, and more than 10 against search alone.

07 · Plan and costTwo phases, the usual gates

Phase 1 · V0.20 · size M

  • Link chips, with the recognition rule and its tests.
  • Lens drawer on the V0.19 story endpoint; desktop drawer, phone sheet.
  • Find-anything palette and a header "Find" button.
  • Display switch for links; training and operator manual sections.
  • Frontend only. No migration, no new route.

InferenceSimilar in size to V0.19's frontend (about 550 lines of interface code plus tests), because it reuses V0.19's story parsing and entries.

Phase 2 · V0.21 · size S to M

  • Watch list: pin, unpin, the strip above every page.
  • "Since you last looked" per user and object.
  • Migration 0021, 3 routes, audit of pins.
  • Only if the Phase 1 test shows the gain.

Moves the roadmap's synopsis and look-ahead releases back one number each.

Each release runs the verification loop, the engineering and security gates, the pipeline simulation, the container smoke and the deploy gate. You upload.

08 · How we will knowMeasure before building, then after shipping

Hallway test, before code

  • 3 analysts, 5 questions each, timed, in the prototype (section 09), which switches between today's Holly and the lens, with synthetic data.
  • Questions such as "What is due next on 90762?" and "Did anyone on the floor discuss the 7afc notice?"
  • Record time, wrong answers and where they got lost.

Success, after shipping

  • Median time to answer at least halved on the 5 questions. Speculationtarget to agree
  • No question needs more than 2 page changes.
  • No rise in wrong answers.

Stop if

  • The hallway test shows no clear gain over today's pages: Phase 1 is shelved and V0.20 returns to the synopsis.
  • Analysts find the links distracting and switch them off: keep the palette and drop the chips.

09 · Prototype and testA working prototype, ready for the hallway test

Built on 17 November 2026: the real V0.19 dashboard on synthetic data, with the lens behind a switch and a facilitator console that runs the test. One offline file; it can be tried below.

What it is

  • Holly's own pages, built from the repository, answered in the browser from synthetic data.
  • The lens on top: number links, the drawer, Find on Ctrl K or /, the watch strip.
  • A switch shows the same file as today's Holly.

What the console records

  • 5 timed tasks per half, one half per condition, on 2 matched objects.
  • Outcome, seconds, page changes, lens and Find opens, link clicks, ease from 1 to 7.
  • Order alternates between participants; results export as CSV.

Checked

  • FactNo network call; synthetic data only.
  • FactAll 10 questions answerable in today's Holly.
  • FactThe "today" half shows no links and no Find.

Try it here

Loads the embedded prototype (about 1 MB) only when asked. It opens on the facilitator set-up; choose Explore freely, lens on to look around. Synthetic data; nothing leaves the page. For the hallway test itself, save it as a file and open that: an embedded copy keeps nothing once the page closes.

Facilitator guide: docs/roadmap/object-lens-hallway-test.md. Source and build: prototypes/object-lens. InferencePrototype code, not gated; the production lens is written into Holly under the usual loop and gates.

10 · Out of scopeWhat this is not

  • No new data source, no change to what Holly pulls or keeps.
  • No language model and nothing sent outside Holly.
  • No change to who can see what.
  • No removal of any page: every tab stays.
  • Not the synopsis, the look-ahead or provider deltas from the Handover roadmap.
